title: Plitvička Jezera Prices 2027: Realistic Daily Budget
metaDescription: Plitvička Jezera 2027 budget: park tickets €10–€40, rooms from about €50, meals, parking and daily totals, plus how prices have shifted since 2025.
content:
## How Much Does Plitvička Jezera Cost in 2027?

A realistic 2027 budget for two adults is €180–€260 per day in shoulder season and €280–€400 per day in July and August. That covers a double room, two park tickets, parking, one restaurant dinner and simpler meals otherwise. Park tickets are the fixed cost. Accommodation is the cost that moves most.

These 2027 figures are projections. They are built on the 2026 tariff and room rates, with a small allowance for inflation of about 3–5%. The park has not confirmed a 2027 tariff yet, so check the official ticket portal before booking.

## How Have Prices Changed Recently?

The park tariff itself has been stable. The 2026 prices are reported as unchanged from 2025. The big jump came earlier, when the summer adult ticket rose to €40 and the park introduced timed entry. Entry is now capped per hour at each entrance, so the practical change for visitors is that tickets must be booked in advance, and peak slots sell out.

The main shifts visitors have noticed:

- **Summer tickets cost four times the winter ticket.** The adult price runs from €10 in winter to €40 in peak summer.
- **A cheaper afternoon ticket exists.** From June to August, entry after 4 pm costs €25 for adults. In September the cut-off is 3 pm.
- **Accommodation is the main source of inflation.** Booking platforms show a 3-star average of roughly $94–$120 (about €85–€110) per night, with 4-star properties near €160–€170 in season.
- **Tourist tax has risen.** Rates of €1.33 per adult per night (April–September) and €0.93 (October–March) appeared on earlier listings. Newer ones show €1.50 for April–September.

Expect a modest further rise in 2027 for lodging and restaurants. A park tariff change is possible but unconfirmed.

## Park Ticket Prices (Base for the 2027 Budget)

Tickets are the same at Entrance 1 and Entrance 2, and each ticket is tied to an entrance and a time slot.

### One-day tickets (2026 tariff)

| Period | Adult | Student | Child 7–18 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jan–Mar, Nov–Dec | €10 | €6 | €4 |
| Apr–May, Oct | €23 | €14 | €6 |
| Jun–Sep | €40 | €25 | €15 |
| Jun–Aug after 4 pm (Sep after 3 pm) | €25 | €15 | €9 |

Children under 7 enter free. Some sites round the shoulder-season adult price to €23.50, so a small difference at checkout is possible.

### Two-day tickets

Adults pay €15 in winter, €39 in spring and October, and €60 in summer. Two afternoon tickets in summer cost €50, but they give fewer usable hours than the €60 two-day ticket. The park allows arrival up to one hour after the ticket time, but not earlier.

Each ticket includes the electric boat on Kozjak and the panoramic train within your chosen route, plus visitor insurance. Nothing extra is charged inside the park for transport.

## Accommodation Costs

The village area of Plitvička Jezera (Jezerce, Mukinje, Poljanak, Plitvica Selo) sits roughly 2–4 km from the park entrances. Most guesthouses are family-run.

- **Budget guesthouses and rooms:** about €45–€80 per night for a double in low and shoulder season. Examples include Guesthouse Bor (Mukinje), Guest House Tone (Poljanak) and Plitvice Miric Inn (Jezerce).
- **Mid-range hotels:** Hotel Jezero has been listed from about €90 and up to €170 in peak periods. Hotel Bellevue and Hotel Plitvice sit near the same bracket. Plitvice Ethno House runs about €100–€125.
- **Higher end:** 4-star properties such as Etno Garden Exclusive Hotel typically start around €150 in season.

For 2027, budget €60–€90 for a guesthouse double in shoulder season and €100–€160 in July and August. Add the tourist tax: €1.50 per adult per night from April to September.

In practice, booking within the national park boundary is rarely worth the premium. The park hotels (Jezero, Bellevue, Plitvice) cost more than village guesthouses with similar ratings, and the walking distance saved is small, since the park shuttle starts at the entrances anyway.

## Food and Drink

Restaurant prices around the park are higher than in inland Croatian towns. Typical ranges in 2026, with 2027 likely 3–5% higher:

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Coffee | €2–€3 |
| Local beer (0.5 l) | €4–€5 |
| Grilled meat or trout main | €13–€22 |
| Pizza or pasta | €10–€14 |
| Lamb or veal under the bell (peka), per portion | €18–€28 |
| Picnic from a supermarket | €6–€10 |

A sit-down dinner for two with a drink each lands at €45–€65. Lunch kiosks inside the park are priced for captive visitors, so a packed lunch saves €10–€15 per person.

## Getting There and Parking

Bus from Zagreb takes about 2 h 30 min, and from Split about 3 h 30 min. Bus fares are typically €12–€20 each way, with more expensive services in summer. Rental cars from Zagreb or Zadar run about €35–€65 per day depending on season and insurance. Zagreb to Plitvice is roughly 130 km.

Parking is charged at both entrances, and summer rates are higher. Budget €7–€10 for a full day in summer, with lower rates off-season. Check the current tariff at the gate.

## Sample 2027 Daily Budgets (Per Person, Two Sharing)

| Style | Winter (Nov–Mar) | Shoulder (Apr–May, Oct) | Summer (Jun–Sep) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Budget | €45–€60 | €70–€90 | €90–€115 |
| Mid-range | €65–€90 | €95–€130 | €140–€200 |
| Comfort | €110–€150 | €150–€200 | €220–€300 |

The budget row assumes a guesthouse room, a packed lunch, a simple dinner and a public bus or shared car. Mid-range assumes a 3-star hotel or better guesthouse, restaurant dinner and a rental car. Comfort assumes a 4-star stay, a two-day ticket and restaurant meals both days.

## Ways to Spend Less

- **Visit in late October or April.** The ticket is €23 instead of €40 and rooms cost 25–40% less than in August.
- **Use the afternoon ticket in summer.** Entry after 4 pm costs €25. Lower Lakes are quieter, and the park is open in the evening light. The catch is limited time, so it suits Route A or a short Lower Lakes loop, not the full lake system.
- **Stay in the villages, not the hotels.** Guesthouses in Jezerce and Mukinje undercut hotels by 30–50%.
- **Book the park slot first, then the room.** Popular summer time slots sell out before rooms do.
- **Skip the tour if you have a car.** Day tours from Zagreb start at about €58 with a ticket, but self-driving with a €40 ticket costs about the same and gives full control over timing.

## Insider Tips

- Book the 7:00 or 8:00 am slot and start with the Lower Lakes. Tour buses tend to arrive around 10 am.
- Winter tickets are cheap at €10, but usually only the Lower Lakes are open, so the value depends on conditions.
- The village of Rastoke in Slunj, about 30–40 minutes away, is free to walk and works as a low-cost add-on.
- Cash is still useful at small guesthouses and for parking, although cards are widely accepted.

## Is Plitvička Jezera Expensive Compared With Other Croatian Destinations?

It is cheaper than Dubrovnik and the Dalmatian coast in July and August, but pricier than Zagreb for equal-quality rooms. The €40 ticket is the largest single cost for many visitors, and it is higher than most national parks in the region. Value improves sharply outside June to September.

faq.question: How much does a day at Plitvice Lakes cost in 2027?
faq.answer: Expect about €90–€130 per person per day in shoulder season and €140–€200 in summer, including a mid-range room share, ticket, parking and meals. Budget travelers can manage €70–€115 using guesthouses and packed lunches.

faq.question: How much is the Plitvice Lakes ticket in 2027?
faq.answer: The 2027 tariff is not confirmed, but 2026 prices are €10 (Nov–Mar), €23 (Apr, May, Oct) and €40 (Jun–Sep) for adults. Summer entry after 4 pm costs €25. Children under 7 enter free.

faq.question: Is Plitvice Lakes more expensive than before?
faq.answer: The park tickets stayed unchanged from 2025 to 2026. Lodging, food and the municipal tourist tax have risen slightly. A further increase of 3–5% in 2027 is a reasonable planning assumption.

faq.question: How much do hotels near Plitvice Lakes cost per night?
faq.answer: Guesthouses cost about €45–€80 per night in low and shoulder season. 3-star hotels average about €85–€110, and 4-star hotels about €160–€170 in season. Summer weekends are the most expensive.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Plitvice Lakes?
faq.answer: November to March has the lowest prices, with a €10 adult ticket and cheap rooms, but only some trails are open. April and October offer the best balance at €23 per ticket with all main areas usually accessible.

faq.question: Is the two-day ticket worth it?
faq.answer: In summer, the €60 two-day ticket suits those who want both Upper and Lower Lakes at a relaxed pace. In winter at €15, it is rarely needed, since one day covers the open trails.

faq.question: Do I have to pay a tourist tax in Plitvička Jezera?
faq.answer: Yes. The municipal tax is about €1.50 per adult per night from April to September, with lower rates for ages 12–17 and in winter. It is usually paid at the accommodation.

quickAnswer: Plan on €90–€130 per person per day in shoulder season and €140–€200 in summer for Plitvička Jezera in 2027. This assumes a guesthouse room share, a park ticket (€23 to €40), parking, and two restaurant meals. Winter visits can drop to roughly €60–€90 per person per day.
